evaluations.rationale: S1 captures basic duties (info, liability, assistance) but omits key rights (compensation percentages, exemption regime, enforcement bodies, security, service‑quality standards). It misstates that assistance for disabled includes meals/accommodation, which belongs to delay rights. Clear language but incomplete and partly inaccurate.

S2 includes core rights (info, delay reimbursement, assistance for disabled) and complaint handling, but adds unsupported details (response‑time limits, recourse claims) and omits exemption rules, security, sanctions and service‑quality standards. Generally clear and useful, though slightly over‑inclusive.

S3 mirrors S1, with the same strengths and gaps: basic duties are covered, but key rights (compensation rates, exemption possibilities, enforcement, security) are missing, and assistance is incorrectly extended to meals/accommodation. Language is clear but the summary is incomplete.

S4 adds correct delay rights (meals, accommodation) and mentions assistance for disabled, improving coverage. It also inserts unrelated carriage‑of‑vehicles rules and omits exemption regime, security, enforcement sanctions, and service‑quality standards. Clear but contains extra, non‑gold material.

Adds many details (devices, notified bodies) not in gold and omits key gold points (risk‑management, remedial measures, Commission guidelines). Language is dense, hard for non‑lawyers, and overly long.
Duplicate of S1; same issues: extra technical scope, missing risk‑management and remedial‑measure provisions, dense wording, and excessive length.

Captures core gold points (CAT, traceability, labeling) and overall purpose, but adds peripheral combined‑product rules and omits risk‑management, remedial‑measure and Commission guideline details. Readable but still technical.
Duplicate of S1; suffers same over‑detail, missing key gold provisions, dense legal language and lack of concision.

Adds many details (pilot studies, cost‑benefit, derogations) not in gold, lowering fidelity; covers core domains and Commission role, but extra unverified content reduces legal salience and concision.
Identical to S1; same strengths and weaknesses.
Contains extra provisions (ownership scope, burden considerations) not in gold; core content present but fidelity reduced.
Generally aligns with gold, captures aim, domains, Commission role, gender/regional aspects; adds pilot‑study/derogation notes not in gold, modestly lowering fidelity but remains clear and concise.

S1 captures most duties (annual data, 90% coverage, 12‑month deadline, quality reports) but misstates start date (2008 vs 2009) and adds inaccurate derogation rule (>10% estimate) and irrelevant committee. Clarity good, but legal meaning distorted.

S2 repeats S1’s errors: wrong start year (2008), introduces >10% derogation, cites Standing Committee not in gold. Covers key data items and reporting but omits evaluation report. Clear prose, yet legal fidelity compromised.

S3 mirrors S2 word‑for‑word, inheriting the same inaccuracies (2008 start, >10% derogation, wrong committee). Includes most required data points but lacks the 3‑year evaluation report. Clear but legally inaccurate.

S4 correctly notes 90% coverage, 1 000 t threshold, 12‑month deadline and reporting duties, but adds exclusions (aquarium, plant species) and a >10% derogation rule not in gold. Misses the 3‑year evaluation report. Clear but deviates from legal text.

Accurately reflects all gold points (aim, data, sources, protection, reference dates, 27‑month deadline, confidentiality, quality report, Commission role). Adds unrelated regulation references (322/97) – not false but not in gold. Dense but clear; a bit long.

Covers main rules, data sources, protection, reference dates and quality reporting. Omits specific 27‑month deadline and first reference year 2011. Adds extra regulation citations and NUTS level detail not in gold. Generally clear and concise.

Essentially identical to S2; same strengths and gaps. Captures core obligations but leaves out deadline specifics and first reference year. Includes unverified regulation references and NUTS detail. Clear enough for non‑lawyers.

Matches gold on aim, data, sources, protection, reference dates and quality reporting. Misses the 27‑month transmission deadline and first reference year. Adds citation to Reg 322/97 (not in gold). Well‑structured, reasonably concise.

Adds exemptions, 28‑day notification, reporting periods and level‑3 training not mentioned in gold; core requirements are present but many extra, non‑gold details lower fidelity and salience. Text is clear but verbose.
Repeats S1’s non‑gold exemptions, 28‑day data‑change rule and bi‑annual reporting. Core rules are covered, but extra unverified details dilute legal fidelity and salience; readability acceptable.

Introduces specific capital amounts, check‑frequency dates and proof‑of‑repute procedures absent from gold. Core conditions are present, but many unverified specifics reduce fidelity and increase length.

Accurately lists main requirements and manager role, but still adds exemptions and reporting timelines not in gold. Presentation is clearer and more focused than other candidates, improving lay clarity and practical grasp.

Contains many provisions not in gold (5‑year limit, candidate‑substitution, 30‑month rule) and omits key 10‑year/15‑year limits, distorting legal meaning; overly detailed, dense, and hard for lay readers.
Duplicate of S1; same issues of extra, inaccurate details and missing core time‑limit information, reducing fidelity and usefulness.
Adds concepts (max residue levels, candidate substitution) absent from gold and omits the 10/15‑year approval periods; extra technicalities dilute core message.

Accurately reflects gold’s core rules (scope, safety criteria, national authority role, mutual recognition) without contradictions; misses explicit 10‑year/15‑year limits but otherwise clear and useful for non‑lawyers.

No conflict with gold (which contains no content). Includes all substantive points of the regulation, prioritises key duties and reporting. Clear but somewhat lengthy; minor redundancy lowers concision and lay clarity.
Consistent with gold (no content). Captures core reporting, data‑collection and reporting cycles. Slightly more legal jargon than S1 but still understandable; length modestly impacts concision.
Accurately reflects regulation; repeats many points, making the text less crisp. Clarity suffers from redundancy, though legal content is intact.
Legally faithful but adds extra procedural detail (crop selection, reference‑period choice) that is not in gold, increasing complexity and reducing brevity and lay readability.

Accurately describes application, competent bodies and fees, but omits key gold points (exclusions, prohibited substances, EUEB, detailed award criteria). No contradictions, but limited coverage reduces legal fidelity and practical understanding.

Covers all gold material: scope, exclusions, prohibited substances, competent bodies, fees, EUEB, criteria, Commission role, reporting. No contradictions. Slightly verbose, but clear for non‑lawyers; good practical picture.
Essentially duplicate of S1; same strengths and gaps. Misses exclusions, prohibited substances and EUEB, limiting coverage despite accurate procedural description.
Similar to S1 with added procedural detail (6‑month deadline) not in gold. Still lacks exclusions, prohibited substances, and EUEB info, so coverage and salience are limited though no contradictions.

Adds many roles (Commission, allocation bodies, shippers) not in gold and omits core elements (executive board, advisory groups, corridor deadlines). Overly long, dilutes key legal structure, reducing fidelity and practical clarity.

Introduces track‑gauge exemption and performance‑scheme monitoring not in gold; misses executive board, advisory groups, corridor deadlines. Provides a readable narrative but adds unsupported provisions, lowering legal fidelity.
Duplicate of S2 with same extra, non‑gold details and missing executive board, advisory groups, corridor dates. Clear language but legal content diverges from reference, harming fidelity.

Captures main structure (boards, one‑stop shop, pre‑arranged paths) but omits corridor deadlines, advisory groups, priority rules, and annex list. Adds a deployment‑plan concept not in gold. Balanced length, fairly clear for non‑lawyers.

Captures most gold points (port‑state control, labeling, lost‑gear, inspection thresholds) but misstates inspection share (15% vs 5%/7.5%). Adds some extra procedural dates not in gold. Overall clear but slightly inaccurate.

Accurate on logbook, coordination and inspection triggers, but omits key gold items (port closures, frozen‑fish labeling, inspection %s, lost‑gear retrieval). Introduces specific deadlines not in gold, which are unconfirmed.
Repeats S2’s core but adds no new gold content. Misses port‑state control, labeling, inspection percentages, gear‑retrieval. Adds procedural details (72‑h inspection) not in gold, so not confirmed.
Similar to S3, adds purpose statement matching gold but still lacks port‑state closure, labeling, inspection %s, gear‑retrieval. Includes unverified deadlines and procedural steps not in gold.
Captures main rights and duties, but adds unreferenced details (occasional services, 5‑day notice) and omits key compensation (50% ticket) and injury protection. Clear language, moderately concise.
Accurately reflects core rights, adds occasional‑service clause not in gold, misses 50% ticket compensation and injury protection. Well‑structured, relatively concise.
Includes core provisions, adds unreferenced limits (EUR 80/night) and occasional‑service scope, omits 50% ticket compensation and injury protection. Clear but slightly verbose.
Matches gold on main rights, repeats occasional‑service clause absent from gold, lacks 50% ticket compensation and injury protection. Clear presentation, concise.
Captures main scope, exclusions and labelling duties, but misstates exemption of tailors, omits language, surveillance, ‘100%’ limits and date. Clear but incomplete.
Accurately reflects gold points and adds many extra details (tolerances, Annex VI) not in gold. No contradictions, but peripheral info lowers salience and makes it less concise.
Same as S2 with additional specifics (‘other fibres’, special cotton‑linen case). No falsehoods, but extra technicalities dilute focus and increase length.
Duplicate of S3; same strengths and weaknesses.
Core sanctions and procedure are correct, but misses start‑date, ESM transfer and Six‑pack context; adds peripheral details (delegated acts, return of deposits) that dilute focus.
Accurately reflects sanctions and reporting, yet omits application date, ESM fund flow and Six‑pack background; includes extra procedural minutiae not in gold.
Correct on main sanctions and 5‑year report, but lacks start‑date, ESM revenue use and Six‑pack context; adds unrelated clauses (special report, delegated acts).
Matches gold on sanctions and reporting, but omits key facts (effective from 13 Dec 2011, ESM transfer, Six‑pack) and inserts extra procedural details not present in the reference.

Captures register, inspections, port denial and some gear rules, but omits most area‑specific closures, red‑coral rules, incidental‑catch provisions and capacity limits. Adds unreferenced weather‑carry‑over and net‑size details.
Repeats S1’s core points and adds reporting dates not in gold. Misses key habitat‑area bans, red‑coral specifics, incidental‑catch rules and stock‑capacity limits, limiting coverage.
Essentially same content as S2; accurate where present but omits most specific spatial/temporal restrictions, red‑coral and incidental‑catch measures, reducing material completeness.

Broadly reflects the regulation’s purpose, scope, vessel register, port‑control and inspection rules. Still lacks many detailed area‑specific bans, red‑coral provisions, incidental‑catch releases and stock‑capacity limits, but overall more complete than S1‑S3.
Accurate core meaning, but omits key exclusions (agricultural, military, public‑admin vehicles) and adds unreferenced 2‑month objection rule. Long and repetitive, reducing concision.
Matches gold on purpose, scope, timelines; misses specific vehicle exclusions and adds procedural details not in gold. Lengthy, affecting concision.
Accurately reflects gold’s core rules, but omits several exclusion categories and inserts a 2‑month objection clause not in gold. Verbose, reducing concision.

Captures aim, scope, Malta exemption, timelines, committee role and repeal of earlier regulation. Still lacks some exclusion details (agricultural, military, admin vehicles) and adds non‑gold specifics, but overall more salient.

Captures all gold points, adds peripheral details (Title XII, specific dates) that are not in the gold but not contradictory. Language is clear enough for an informed non‑lawyer, though somewhat verbose.
Reflects gold content accurately; repeats many points and adds unreferenced procedural specifics. Still clear for a lay audience, but length reduces concision.
Matches gold’s substance, with extra references (Title XII, deadline) that are not in the gold but not false. Presentation is readable yet repetitive, affecting brevity.
Accurately conveys gold information, adds non‑gold procedural details (e.g., specific dates). Clear enough for non‑lawyers, but the text is lengthy and somewhat redundant.
Accurately reflects gold points, adds unreferenced details, dense legal language reduces clarity and concision.
Same as S1 – correct core content, but overly technical and verbose.
Identical to S1/S2; same strengths and weaknesses.
Same content as other candidates; accurate but overly detailed and not user‑friendly.

Legal fidelity: no direct conflict but adds many details not in gold. Material coverage: omits aim, optional terms, exclusions, dates. Salience: focuses on registration mechanics rather than overall framework. Clarity: dense but understandable. Practical: gives process info but misses key policy points. Concision: overly long.

Fidelity OK, but adds unreferenced transitional rules. Misses regulation’s aim, optional quality terms, exclusions, and key dates. Emphasises registration details over main scheme features. Clear enough for lay reader, but still dense. Moderately concise.

Same content as S2; same strengths and gaps. No contradictions, but many gold points absent (aim, optional terms, exclusions, dates). Focus on registration process. Reasonably clear, but not concise enough for a public summary.

Accurately reflects gold: aims, scope, exclusions, labeling, optional quality terms, transitional periods, entry‑into‑force dates. No contradictions. Highlights key legal points, clear language for non‑lawyers. Slightly verbose but stays focused.

Covers main aims, budget, Greek role, checks and penalties, but adds unverified claims (Crete/Evia exception, product quality limits, correlation table). Lengthy and includes peripheral details, reducing concision.
Identical to S1; same strengths and weaknesses – accurate core content but introduces unverified details and is overly long.
Includes gold’s key points and is slightly shorter, but still adds unverified statements (exclusion of Crete/Evia, quality criteria, delegated acts). Overall fidelity moderate.
Accurately reflects aims, budget, Greek/Commission roles, and checks, yet asserts prohibitions and quality limits not in gold. Lengthy with extra peripheral info, lowering concision.
Accurately reflects gold criteria, list cycle, coordinators and funding, but adds many procedural details not in gold, making it less focused and harder for lay readers.
Covers gold’s main points (criteria, list renewal) but omits funding and size of PCI list; adds many technical provisions, reducing salience and concision.
Reflects gold’s criteria and list cycle but lacks mention of €6 bn CEF funding and the 248 projects; includes extensive procedural detail not in gold.
Matches gold on criteria and list renewal but omits funding and project count; adds unrelated network‑plan details, lowering focus and brevity.

Focuses on law‑enforcement comparison rules, omits core asylum‑fingerprint collection, 72‑hour deadline, age 14 threshold, data erasure on citizenship and non‑EU sharing limits. Adds unverified provisions (third‑country transfers). Dense legal language reduces lay clarity.

Captures asylum‑responsibility aim, age 14 rule and law‑enforcement conditions, but states a 10‑year storage/automatic erasure rule not in gold (gold says erase on citizenship). Otherwise clear and reasonably concise.

Mentions updates on arrival/departure and a three‑year block after protection, which contradicts gold (erasure on citizenship). Misses 72‑hour transmission, age threshold, and law‑enforcement ‘last resort’ condition. Language is fairly clear but coverage is weak.
Accurately notes asylum‑responsibility purpose, age 14 rule and law‑enforcement conditions, but adds a 10‑year automatic erasure rule not in gold. Otherwise clear, concise and covers main points.

Captures main aim and goods scope, but adds unreferenced actors (collective bodies, third‑country cooperation) and misstates non‑application to “goods released for free”. Misses IPR list, small‑consignment rules, destruction conditions. Lengthy with peripheral details, reducing salience and concision.

Identical to S1; same strengths and weaknesses. Provides correct overall picture but includes unsupported claims and omits key IPR categories, small‑consignment and destruction specifics. Overly detailed on non‑essential points, hurting salience and brevity.

Accurately reflects procedural steps, notification timelines and data‑exchange, improving clarity. Lacks the exhaustive IPR list, small‑consignment definition and destruction‑without‑proceedings rule. Adds a one‑day notice rule not in gold, so some unconfirmed detail.

Covers customs scope, IPR types and application data, and destruction process, but introduces timelines (10/3 days) and data‑retention periods not in gold. Omits small‑consignment rules and the specific destruction‑without‑court condition. Balanced length but includes unverified specifics.
Preserves gold’s aim, importance, implementing act and date; adds many peripheral details (NUTS, feasibility studies, other regs, cease date) that do not distort but lower salience and concision.
Accurately reflects gold’s core points; adds extra provisions (NUTS, feasibility funding, other regs, cease date) that are not in gold, reducing salience and making it less concise.
Matches gold’s legal meaning; introduces detailed data breakdowns and other references absent from gold, which are peripheral and affect concision.
Faithfully conveys gold’s core content; adds extensive ancillary provisions (principles, financial support, other regs) not in gold, lowering salience and making it less concise.

Budget figure (€84.936bn) contradicts gold (€99.3bn) – legal fidelity reduced. Misses COVID‑19 emergency aid, 2017 amendment details, and full priority list, limiting coverage. Includes many definitions not in gold (noise). Clear language but verbose, reducing concision.

Repeats budget error (€84.936bn vs €99.3bn) and omits COVID‑19 aid, 2017 amendment, and transitional rules, lowering fidelity and coverage. Adds network details not in gold. Language is clear but overly detailed, hurting concision.
Same budget inaccuracy and missing COVID‑19, 2017 amendment, and budget breakdown as gold. Includes extra technical definitions. Clear for lay readers but verbose, reducing concision.

No factual contradictions, but omits key gold elements: budget amount, COVID‑19 emergency aid, 2017 amendment, and full priority list. Adds peripheral details (flat‑rate aid) not in gold. Clear and concise, but coverage gaps lower overall scores.
Core objectives and eligible actions are present, but the summary adds unreferenced dates, procedural timelines and rights not in the gold, omits the budget, and is overly long, reducing concision.
Reflects the main aims and actions, yet repeats unverified details (e.g., dates, Justice programme exclusion, specific rights) and lacks budget info; still fairly clear but somewhat verbose.
Core objectives are covered, but many added elements (Annex III, subsidiarity, EU bodies) are not in the gold; budget omitted; length and peripheral details lower salience and concision.
Mirrors S3; includes extra, unreferenced procedural and institutional details, omits budget, and is verbose, reducing legal fidelity and concision while still conveying the main purpose.

Focuses narrowly on national programmes and reporting, omits many gold points (principles, EU actions, info/publicity rules). Adds unreferenced deadlines. Clear language but verbose; limited overall picture.
Repeats S1 with extra eligibility detail not in gold. Still misses core aims, principles, EU‑wide actions. Clear but repetitive; adds unverified specifics.
Identical to S2; same strengths and gaps. Over‑focus on programme mechanics, lacks broader fund context, principles, and emergency assistance.
Covers most gold points (principles, EU actions, reporting, control, technical assistance). Adds some extra references not in gold but not contradictory. Dense but conveys purpose and scope well.

Captures main objectives and resettlement lump‑sum but adds unsupported claims (e.g., applies to third countries, Commission ‘user‑friendly’ implementation). Misses Denmark exception, budget, start date. Lengthy, some peripheral detail reduces salience and concision.

Accurately reflects the four objectives, national programmes, annex‑II actions and resettlement lump sums. Adds reporting deadline and eligibility details not in gold but not contradictory. Omits Denmark exception, budget figure and start date. Clear enough for non‑lawyers.

Same core content as S2 with extra integration‑capacity‑building details not in gold. No contradictions. Still lacks Denmark, budget, start date. Lengthier and denser, reducing lay clarity and concision.

Repeats gold objectives but introduces false claim that Member States must allocate at least 20 % of resources to certain objectives. Omits Denmark exception, budget, start date. Extra detail and inaccuracy lower legal fidelity and overall usefulness.

S1 captures the overall aim and many supervisory duties but omits key fee‑cap rules, 15 % income threshold, audit‑committee approval for non‑audit services, appointment mechanics, audit‑report specifics and transitional limits. It adds a non‑existent exemption right. The text is dense and repetitive, reducing concision.

S2 mentions the aim and supervisory powers but leaves out fee‑structure limits, 15 % income rule, audit‑committee approval, appointment process, audit‑report format, transparency‑report details and transitional provisions. It adds a broad exemption clause not in the gold. Overall readability is acceptable but legal substance is thin.

S3 overstates the ban on non‑audit services (gold allows some with audit‑committee approval) and omits fee caps, 15 % income threshold, appointment rules, audit‑report details, transparency‑report and transitional measures. The rest aligns loosely with the gold, but the distortion lowers legal fidelity.

S4 also asserts a blanket prohibition on non‑audit services, contrary to the gold’s conditional ban. It misses fee‑cap rules, 15 % income trigger, detailed appointment mechanics, audit‑report structure, transparency‑report specifics and transitional limits. The added definitional list is not in the gold.

Accurately reflects gold’s core rules, measures and criteria; adds no contradictory facts. Covers all material points, though includes peripheral details (e.g., confidentiality). Dense legal language reduces lay clarity and concision.
Faithful to gold, includes all key provisions and criteria. Slightly more concise than S1 but still verbose; legal jargon hampers lay readability. No false statements.
Captures gold’s substance, adds reporting and confidentiality details not in gold but not contradictory. Lengthy and repetitive, limiting clarity and concision, but legal meaning preserved.

Accurately mirrors gold, includes all major measures and criteria. Adds some procedural extras (consultations, confidentiality) that are peripheral. Still verbose, affecting lay clarity and concision.
S1 captures all gold points, adds many article details, no contradictions. Dense legal language reduces lay clarity and concision.
S2 mirrors gold summary closely, clear language, includes objectives, Frontex role, interception, rescue, non‑refoulement and solidarity mechanisms.
S3 repeats S1 content; accurate but overly technical, low readability and concision.
S4 covers gold points, adds proportionality language; reasonably clear but slightly verbose.

Focuses on MiFID‑II provisions and third‑country CSD recognition, omitting the regulation’s core aims (T+2 settlement, book‑entry, settlement‑discipline regime, passporting, prudential rules). No contradictions but major gaps reduce fidelity and usefulness.

Describes CSD authorisation, third‑country recognition and complaint procedures, but leaves out settlement‑period shortening, book‑entry mandate, cash‑penalty regime and passport system. Provides some framework insight yet misses the regulation’s main safety‑efficiency measures.

Captures the regulation’s purpose, CSD governance, record‑keeping, ESMA register and sanction powers. Misses specific T+2 deadline, book‑entry timing, detailed cash‑penalty rules and passporting. Overall clear and useful for non‑lawyers.

Repeats many points of S2 with added access‑criteria details, yet still omits the regulation’s hallmark features (T+2 settlement, mandatory book‑entry, settlement‑discipline cash penalties, EU‑wide passport). Provides procedural info but lacks core substance.

Captures some procedural rules and group coordination but omits key gold points (Denmark exemption, main‑interest jurisdiction presumption, insolvency registers, preventive proceedings). Adds unreferenced details, dense wording reduces clarity and concision.
Identical to S1; same strengths and gaps. Misses several gold‑summary items and includes unverified provisions, making it less useful for non‑lawyers and less faithful to the reference.

Broadly follows gold: aims, jurisdiction, applicable law, registers, group coordination, amendments. Lacks Denmark exemption and some preventive‑proceeding detail, and adds some non‑gold specifics, but overall clear and fairly concise.

Similar to S1/S2; repeats core procedural rules but omits Denmark exemption, register system, preventive proceedings, and main‑interest presumption. Adds unreferenced clauses, resulting in limited clarity and excess length.

The summary accurately describes conformity‑assessment duties and CE‑marking but omits the regulation’s core scope (new installations, modifications), safety‑analysis/report requirement, exclusions, dates and penalty rules. No contradictions, but many gold points missing, making it less useful for a lay reader.

Repeats S1’s focus on subsystems and market rules, adding importer details but still lacking the regulation’s overall scope, safety‑report duties, exemptions, entry‑into‑service dates and penalty provisions. No false statements, yet key gold content absent.

Covers the full scope (new installations, modifications, subsystems, exemptions), safety‑analysis/report, manufacturer duties, documentation period, conformity bodies, penalties and dates. Language is clear though dense; overall concise and accurate for non‑lawyers.

Essentially a duplicate of S1/S2, focusing on subsystem market rules while omitting the regulation’s broader installation scope, safety‑report requirement, exemptions, dates and penalty framework. No contradictions but many gold points missing.

Accurately states lawful bases, supervisory powers and scope, but omits many gold‑point rights (portability, erasure, breach notice) and key business rules (DPO, one‑stop shop, design‑by‑default, SME exemptions). Legal language heavy, limiting lay clarity.

Covers scope, individual rights list, record‑keeping, supervisory board and transfer adequacy. Misses DPO requirement, one‑stop shop, design‑by‑default, pseudonymisation, SME exemption details. Generally clear and useful for non‑lawyers.

Duplicate of S1; same strengths and gaps. Accurate on lawful bases and supervisory roles but lacks individual‑rights details and many business‑rule items from gold. Dense legal phrasing reduces lay readability.

Captures many gold points (scope, DPO, SME exemption, transfer safeguards) and is clearly written. Misses explicit rights list and design‑by‑default, pseudonymisation. Slight inaccuracy on law‑enforcement regime reference.

Focuses heavily on data‑protection rules not mentioned in the gold and omits core tasks (threat assessments, joint teams, cyber‑centre). Some statements are correct but add unreferenced details, reducing fidelity and coverage.
Repeats data‑protection focus of S1, adds no new gold‑based content, and leaves out many listed objectives and tasks. Extra provisions on transfers are not in the reference, lowering fidelity.
Captures objectives, tasks, oversight, data‑protection role, and applicability dates from the gold. Language is slightly legalistic but clear enough; no contradictory or unreferenced claims.
Essentially a duplicate of S1; over‑emphasises data‑protection details absent from the gold and omits key operational tasks, resulting in low fidelity and coverage.

Legal fidelity moderate – core aim and vessel scope present, but adds unreferenced details (50% capacity, 2% margin) that may mislead. Covers many gold points yet omits sanctions and 1‑year termination rule. Salient points diluted by peripheral clauses. Dense legal language reduces lay clarity and concision.

Introduces inaccurate concepts (non‑market‑economy focus, “Union industry”) not in gold, lowering fidelity. Misses vessel‑size thresholds, sanctions, 1‑year limit. Over‑emphasises procedural rights, making salient content less clear. Language heavy, long, and omits key practical details.

Contains unreferenced clauses (loan‑security exemption) and omits key gold items (vessel size, sanctions, 1‑year termination). Core aim is present but distorted by extra, unsupported details. Dense phrasing hampers lay readability; overall coverage is partial and not concise.

Duplicate of S2 with same inaccuracies (non‑market‑economy focus, “Union industry”) and missing vessel‑size, sanctions, termination limits. Adds unsupported procedural specifics, reducing legal fidelity and salience. Lengthy and legalistic, limiting lay clarity and concision.
No contradictions, but omits core conditions, complaint procedure, timelines and types of measures. Focuses on market‑economy rules not highlighted in gold, reducing material coverage and salience.

Accurate on market‑economy and undertaking rules, but still misses the four‑condition test, filing steps, 45‑day review, provisional/definitive duty timelines and amendment details. Adds a 7‑8‑month timeline not in gold.
Duplicate of S2; same strengths and gaps. Correct on procedural aspects it mentions, but omits the fundamental conditions, complaint filing, duty types, and amendment specifics.

Captures investigation mechanics, parties’ rights, provisional measures and refund, aligning with gold. Misses the four‑condition test, complaint filing details, exact timelines, and amendment nuances, but overall preserves the main legal effect.

Captures many obligations (plans, capacity, by‑catch, observer, caging) but omits key gold points (size limits, biomass target, sport‑catch specifics, marketing docs). Adds unreferenced details (camera systems, 10‑day investigation) that are not contradictory but not in gold. Text is long and dense, reducing clarity and concision.

Identical to S1; same strengths and gaps. Provides many procedural rules but misses size limits, biomass goal, sport‑fishing caps and marketing documentation. Inserts specifics not in gold (camera, 10‑day rule). Lengthy and repetitive, hurting lay readability and concision.

Focuses on deadlines and reporting obligations, matching gold on plans, capacity, farming, observer and caging. Lacks size reference, biomass target, sport‑catch limits and marketing rules. Adds a 10 % difference trigger not in gold. More concise and clearer than S1/S2, improving lay clarity.

Covers most gold points: by‑catch limit, sport‑fishing release, record‑keeping, observer, marketing docs, caging, ports, and overall recovery aim. Misses explicit size limits and the 60 % probability/MSY biomass target. Adds a generic sustainability statement not in gold. Well‑structured, fairly concise, good for non‑lawyers.

Adds non‑gold elements (consultation forum, specific dates, alternative database use) and omits core A‑G label scale, exclusions, defeat‑device ban, assessment deadline. Lengthy and partly inaccurate, reducing legal fidelity and coverage.

Repeats S1’s extra details (consultation forum, dates) and misses key points such as the A‑G scale, second‑hand exclusion, defeat‑device ban, and 2025 assessment. Still conveys basic obligations, but legal fidelity is low.

Introduces consent for updates (not in gold) and omits label scale, exclusions, defeat‑device ban, rescaling, and 2025 report. Clear language gives good practical sense, but legal content is incomplete.

Captures purpose, exclusions, database and delegated acts, but adds unsupported deadlines (10‑day docs, 14‑day label replacement) and lacks A‑G scale, defeat‑device ban, 2025 assessment. Generally clear for lay readers.
S1 captures core purpose, assessment steps, transparency and database, but omits detailed public‑interest list and post‑adoption monitoring; adds peripheral info on info‑exchange.
S2 mirrors S1, adds health‑sector example, still lacks explicit public‑interest categories and monitoring after adoption; extra details are not in gold but not contradictory.
Identical to S2; same strengths and gaps.
Duplicate of S2/S3; same evaluation.

Legal fidelity moderate – includes correct 2030 target and transport share but adds details (e.g., 2‑year transport electricity period) not in gold. Misses key heating/cooling and self‑consumption rights, so material coverage low. Focuses on electricity/biofuels, omitting several salient points. Language is dense but understandable; practical rules

Captures overall 32 % target, self‑consumer rights and transport 14 % target, but omits heating/cooling specifics and district‑heating rights. Adds extra procedural details (5‑year assessments, mass‑balance) not in gold but not contradictory. Clear prose, decent practical picture.

Very similar to S1: correct 2030 overall target and transport 14 % share, but lacks heating/cooling increase, self‑consumption rights and biofuel caps. Introduces some non‑gold details (additionality framework). Dense wording reduces clarity; practical impact partially covered.

Broadly matches gold: 32 % EU target, self‑consumption rights, heating/cooling rules, transport 14 % target, biofuel sustainability criteria, administrative simplification, and third‑country electricity rules. No contradictions; minor missing detail on 1.3 pp heating increase. Clear enough for non‑lawyers.

Captures main aim, scope, exclusions and data deadlines, but adds inaccurate delegated‑act powers and Annex VI reference not in gold. Misses pilot‑study timeline and reporting schedule. Clear language, moderately concise.

Repeats S1’s content and adds further unreferenced procedural details (cost‑effectiveness analysis, 2‑month objection period). Still covers core points but omits pilot studies and reporting deadlines. Clear but slightly verbose.

Essentially identical to S2, with the same unverified delegated‑act and procedural claims. Core scope and data rules are present, but pilot‑study and reporting details are missing. Language is understandable.
